9	 * rule out any positional/count-dependent difference, and there is none): no inter-segment gap
10	 * (`flex items-center`, no gap class), equal-width segments (`flex-[1_0_0]`, an exact match for
11	 * this file's own `flex: '1 0 0'` below), and the active segment always painted with Figma's
12	 * `border/focus` token, every other segment with `border/secondary` — regardless of which index
13	 * is selected. `--zimm-scale-025` (1px height) was already correct from Step 1.
14	 *
15	 * Two parts:
16	 *   - `root` — the full-width flex strip, exactly `--zimm-scale-025` (1px) tall.
17	 *   - `dot` — one equal-width segment per image (despite the part name, this renders as a
18	 *     rectangle in a hairline, not a circular dot — the name matches this component's
19	 *     already-agreed contract, not a literal shape description).
20	 */
21	export const ZimmSlideIndicator = {
22	  parts: ['root', 'dot'],
23	
24	  baseStyle: ({ isActive }: { isActive?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
25	    root: {
26	      display: 'flex',
27	      // Fluid, not a fixed Figma px width — matches the product card's own "fluid, not 288px"
28	      // rule: this strip always spans whatever width its image parent gives it, rather than
29	      // the specific 159.11px/99.44px bounding boxes the two sampled Figma variants happened
30	      // to measure at their own artboard widths.
31	      width: '100%',
32	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-025)', // 1px, confirmed correct since Step 1.
33	      // Confirmed no gap: Figma's own `flex items-center` has no gap class — segments are
34	      // genuinely flush-adjacent, not merely left at a default pending confirmation.
35	      gap: 0,
36	    },
37	
38	    dot: {
39	      // Confirmed exact match: Figma's own `flex-[1_0_0]` on every segment, regardless of count
40	      // or which one is active.
41	      flex: '1 0 0',
42	      height: '100%',
43	      // Both previously read from the wrong semantic alias — `--zimm-color-bg-05` and
44	      // `--zimm-color-opacity-40` happened to LOOK plausible (the active one even resolves to
45	      // the identical hex, since bg-05 and border-focus both trace to the same grey/900
46	      // primitive) but were never actually confirmed against the design, per this file's own
47	      // prior comment. Confirmed via `get_design_context`: the active segment's colour matches
48	      // Figma's `border/focus` token; every other segment matches `border/secondary` — a flat,
49	      // opaque light grey, notably lighter than the semi-transparent overlay `opacity-40`
50	      // previously produced. The active branch below reads `--zimm-color-bg-05`, not
51	      // `--zimm-color-border-focus` — a `border.*` alias is the wrong token *category* for a
52	      // `background` CSS property even though both resolve to the identical grey/900 hex (see
53	      // `foundation/colour.ts`); `border.secondary` has no `background.*` counterpart to swap
54	      // to, so the inactive branch keeps referencing it directly. Both remain
55	      // already-registered tokens, not new ones.
56	      background: isActive ? 'var(--zimm-color-bg-05)' : 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)',
57	    },
58	  }),
59	};
